capture.final_message:
Use the standard entourage description of the compact-convergence uniformity: its basic entourages require
\[
(f(x),g(x))\in V
\]
for every \(x\) in some compact subset of the domain.

For the first conjunct, compactness of \(\alpha\) lets one take that compact subset to be all of \(\alpha\). Thus any basis \(V_i\) of the uniformity on \(\beta\) induces exactly the displayed basis of uniform convergence on \(\alpha\).

For the right side of the equivalence, first view the usual compact-convergence basis as indexed by pairs \((C,m)\), where \(C\subseteq\alpha\) is compact and \(V_m\) is an entourage. The compact exhaustion is cofinal among compact subsets, while the antitone basis \(V_n\) is cofinal among entourages. The diagonal family \((K_n,V_n)\) is therefore cofinal in this paired basis: choose \(n\) large enough that \(C\subseteq K_n\) and \(n\ge m\); antitonicity then gives \(V_n\subseteq V_m\). Its antitonicity follows from \(K_n\subseteq K_{n+1}\) and the decreasing nature of \(V_n\).

The left side of the equivalence is simply the coercion compatibility of `ContinuousMap.toUniformOnFunIsCompact` with `UniformOnFun.toFun`, proved by definitional reduction or function extensionality. Hence both sides of the `Iff` can be established independently, and the equivalence assembled from those two facts. The essential assumptions are compactness in the first statement and the cofinal compact exhaustion plus antitonicity in the diagonal-basis statement.
